headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Notion AI can read shared workspace pages while Chatwoot has broad egress, creating leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system over workspace content, and Chatwoot can ingest customer messages/reports and send them to integrations. If Chatwoot content is copied into Notion pages, prompt-like instructions can traverse the shared workspace. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so interaction risk is more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are pasted into Notion pages that Notion AI later summarizes or answers over
IF workspace content contains attacker-controlled instructions that Notion AI treats as grounded context
mitigations: Mark imported Chatwoot text as untrusted in Notion pages
Strip instructions from support transcripts before saving them to the workspace
Use a separate Notion database for raw transcripts
Add a review step before Notion AI-generated summaries are reused
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to workspace content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, messages, and reports, while Notion AI can access workspace pages and team knowledge base content. Because Notion is vendor-hosted and Chatwoot has broad network egress, sensitive support data can flow into a third-party AI workspace without a strong isolation boundary. The pair therefore creates a realistic leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF support transcripts or reports from Chatwoot are stored in Notion workspace pages
IF Notion AI is allowed to answer over pages containing customer data or interaction history
mitigations: Keep customer transcripts out of Notion AI-indexed pages
Redact identifiers before copying support content into Notion
Restrict Notion pages with customer data to a separate workspace
Disable AI on sensitive databases where possible
requires-engineering: enforce data-class labels and AI access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot exposes API integrations and broad egress, while Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances but no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation. There is overlap on mutable workspace content, yet the profiles do not show both agents writing the same low-level resource concurrently. The conflict is possible but limited to user-managed pages rather than system state.
conditions: IF both agents are used to edit the same Notion page or database record
IF Chatwoot-derived content is manually synchronized into shared workspace pages
mitigations: Assign one agent as the source of truth for each page
Avoid simultaneous edits to the same workspace record
Use page locks or edit windows for shared content
Keep Chatwoot outputs read-only in Notion
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking for synced records

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is explicitly a grounded Q&A/summarization tool, so it may treat Chatwoot-derived notes as authoritative if they are placed in the workspace. Chatwoot can generate reports and messages that downstream users may copy into Notion, creating a path where unverified support content becomes the basis for further actions. The pair can amplify mistakes even without direct automation.
conditions: IF Chatwoot reports are pasted into Notion and then reused as source material
IF Notion AI summaries are acted on without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Notion AI summaries
Keep raw Chatwoot outputs separate from decision documents
Add source links next to every imported support fact
Use a checklist to verify claims before publishing
requires-engineering: add citation enforcement for workspace AI outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data and interaction history, while Notion AI stores and processes workspace pages through vendor backends and downstream model providers. The profiles do not specify residency or retention guarantees for either side, so a compliance mismatch is plausible for regulated customer data. Because the exact jurisdictional mismatch is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is copied into Notion workspace pages
IF the workspace is subject to residency, retention, or deletion obligations
mitigations: Keep regulated records out of Notion AI workspaces
Use a separate compliant system for customer records
Minimize retention of copied support content
Document deletion/export workflows for both tools
requires-engineering: verify residency and retention terms with vendors
